_comment: Orchestrator-owned and FROZEN. External figures the submission is permitted to state, each with its source. `pnpm audit:claims` passes a number in three cases only: it appears in eval/report.json (measured), it appears here (cited), or it is structural (versions, dates, worker ids, list numbering). Anything else fails the build, printing token, file and line.
_note_to_w11: docs/** is your glob, but this file is frozen and the frozen check runs first. You cannot add a citation to justify a number you wrote. If a figure you need is genuinely missing, open `CONTRACT: citation <figure>`. Our own results are never listed here — they come from eval/report.json or they do not ship.

70.source: The Hackett Group — median AP auto-match rate
70.use: The plateau we position against. Cash-application automation reliably reaches roughly 70% touchless and stalls there.

32.6.source: Ardent Partners — average touchless invoice processing rate
32.6.use: The gap between vendor marketing and the median buyer's reality.

49.2.source: Ardent Partners — best-in-class touchless invoice processing rate
49.2.use: Even best-in-class leaves half the work to people.

60.source: SAP cash application — reported plateau range, lower bound of 60-70%
60.use: Corroborates the plateau from the incumbent's own numbers.

95.source: Vendor marketing — upper bound of claimed auto-match rates
95.use: Cited as a claim, never as a fact. Nobody publishes what it cost in wrong matches.

99.8.source: BenchRec, ICAIF 2023 (Operartis) — required match precision, lower bound
99.8.use: Our design principle, stated by a bank three years before this hackathon: leaving a transaction unmatched for review is better than matching it incorrectly.

99.9.source: BenchRec, ICAIF 2023 (Operartis) — required match precision, upper bound
99.9.use: As above. We do not claim to meet it; we state the gap.

92.source: Kognitos — marketing copy conceding an aggressive touchless rate
92.use: A competitor concedes 92% reached by aggressive matching is worse than an honest 85%.

85.source: Kognitos — the honest rate it prefers to an aggressive 92%

91.3.source: OpenSanctions Pairs, February 2026 — rule-based matcher F1
91.3.use: Rules over-match. This is why our deterministic layer is floored on precision, not coverage.

99.0.use: LLMs fail differently, and pairwise matching is near a practical ceiling — so attention should shift to uncertainty-aware review. That is Holdfast.

0.05.source: Duplicate-payment loss estimates — low end of the self-reported range, % of AP spend
0.05.use: The range runs 0.05%-5% and every figure in it is self-reported by firms selling recovery. The variance IS the argument; we cite the spread, never a point estimate.

5.source: OpenAI GPT-5 (model string `gpt-5`), and separately: duplicate-payment loss estimates, high end of the self-reported range (% of AP spend)
5.use: GPT-5 is the STRONG LLM baseline, run on both the selection and holdout sets so the comparison table is like-for-like. A handicapped baseline dies under one question, so the baseline gets the frontier model and the full candidate set.

30.source: Recovery-audit practice — duplicates as share of recovery claims, lower bound of 30-40%
30.use: Why the amount cap exists: duplicates concentrate in high-value invoices.

40.source: Recovery-audit practice — duplicates as share of recovery claims, upper bound

4.7.source: Z.ai GLM-4.7-Flash, served via TensorMux (model string `glm-4-7-flash`)
4.7.use: The residual-proposal model at the LLM boundary. Deliberately not a frontier model: every proposal is re-scored by engine/match and discarded if it does not clear on its own merits, so a weak proposer is a fair test of the gate rather than a handicap.

4.1.source: OpenAI GPT-4.1 — available on the account but NOT used
4.1.use: Recorded only so that a reader who inspects the model catalogue knows which model was chosen and which was passed over.
